The ending of the story feels purposeful, natural, and earned. Throughout the narrative, the protagonist experiences a sense of disorientation, alienation, and uncertainty in the hospital, feeling disconnected from her surroundings and even the baby initially placed in her arms. The central conflict—the mix-up of the babies—builds steadily through subtle clues (the missing birthmark, the unfolded ear, the hospital's general chaos, and finally the hospital bracelet). 

Rather than ending abruptly when the protagonist discovers the truth, the story takes the time to explore her surprising emotional resolution: an overwhelming, undeniable sense of happiness and belonging with the baby she brought home. Her final line to her husband ("I feel... as though we brought home exactly who we were supposed to") brings complete thematic and emotional closure to her character arc, resolving her earlier anxiety and solidifying her choice to keep the child as her own.
